findings.label: Mutation evidence is not in the commit
findings.detail: findings.md and plan.md under .agents/tasks/routing-test-design-20261002/ are untracked, while the committed change-authority-matrix.md row says "Full table in .agents/tasks/routing-test-design-20261002/findings.md". The commit carries only three files. git ls-files .agents reports 83 tracked artefacts including findings.md and plan.md for eight other tasks, so the convention is to track them. Stage both (plus routing-review.md and review.json) so the durable audit row cites a path that exists in the repository.

findings.label: Two by-name negatives sit after the set-equality
findings.detail: tests/test_legacy_redirect_rollback_snapshot.py keeps the /obsolete-login-fixture (line 191) and /workspace (line 192) assertions after assert client.written == approved + rewrites (line 189). The new derived loop at 183 is correctly placed. In the M11 scenario the two still run because that equality is self-consistent, but M10 shows a reordering mutation failing the equality first, so a compound reorder-plus-reinstate would never reach them. Move them above line 189, or drop the commit message's claim that by-name negatives are placed BEFORE every set-equality.

findings.label: Passthrough shadowing uses a raw string prefix
findings.detail: In test_no_ratified_redirect_can_shadow_a_passthrough_or_target_the_staff_tree, source.startswith(PASSTHROUGH_PREFIXES) and passthrough.startswith(stem) are plain string-prefix comparisons. Measured: /getting-started, /api-docs and /mcp-legacy are rejected by the forward branch and /r by the reverse branch, none of which can match an Amplify passthrough pattern (patterns are matched as given, not normalised - the file's own /zip/ entry states this). That reintroduces, in narrow form, the reddening-on-legitimate-product-change failure this redesign exists to end. It fails closed with a precise message. Fix by comparing on segment boundaries (prefix, or prefix + '/'). PASSTHROUGH_PREFIXES already carries the slash for /r/ but not for /api, /get or /mcp.
